messages.subject: [GenABEL-dev] ProbABEL v.0.2.2 released
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have just released version 0.2.2 of ProbABEL. See the release
announcement at http://www.genabel.org/node/266 for more info. This
version is a small upgrade of v0.2.0 with a few bug fixes and mostly
some new functionality in probabel.pl and the ProbABEL config file.

Version 0.2.1 was never released on www.genabel.org, but appeared
briefly in the GenABEL Ubuntu PPA. Unfortunately that version didn't
build correctly. Since PPA's don't allow re-uploading of original source
tar.gz files (to make sure packages always upgrade correctly) I had to
bump the version to 0.2.2 to get the correct version uploaded.

Now that this version is out, Maarten Kooyman and I will focus on
getting the ProbABEL-refactoring branch promoted to trunk. Results so
far a promising in terms of speed gains! Let's see how easy (or not) it
is to merge between and SVN trunk and a branch (and back again).


Best regards,

Lennart.
-- 
-----------------------------------------------------------------
L.C. Karssen
Utrecht
The Netherlands

lennart at karssen.org
http://blog.karssen.org

messages.subject: [GenABEL-dev] The GenABEL suite and AutoMM
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

I would like to inform you about the AutoMM software project. Together with
Diego Fabregat-Traver and prof. Paolo Bientinesi (who are the main
contributors) we worked on speeding up the mixed-model based analysis
(similar to what MixABEL::GWFGLS and GenABEL::mmscore), but also
specifically tailored to the analysis of multiple traits (e.g. 'omics'
data). The software is going to be released under LGPL.

Given shared scope and compatible license, we thought that it may be good
to distribute AutoMM as part of the GenABEL project - both for AutoMM and
for the GenABEL project.

Let us know what you think.

best wishes,
also on behalf of Diego and Paolo,
Yurii

messages.subject: [GenABEL-dev] The GenABEL suite and AutoMM
messages.body_plain:
Dear Yurii and others,

That sounds like a great opportunity! This can maybe help us out with
the lipidomics data we have in our group, and maybe later also with
results from expression studies...

Could you already share some details about AutoMM? Which programming
language was used (C/C++ I assume)? Which (af any) dependencies does it
have? Any idea as to when we can expect to see AutoMM "in person"?

Something that also comes to mind is how are we going to integrate
AutoMM into the family? For example, in terms of input and output file
formats, options (option names) etc.

As to the license, I'm glad to see that an open source license was
chosen for the project!


Lennart.
